item.content:encoded:
1. The words I all made up on the spot so any pronunciation goes, lmao.
  2. I imagine most human interpretations have the Koru-teusa as humanoids with alien characteristics and arm counts corresponding to their numbers. Alien interpretations would be similar, just with their respective anatomies applied instead.
  3. All different species, all non-humanoid (humanoid aliens are boring). In my conception they didn't retain a corporeal form, instead become divine masses of thaumatic radiance, but they summon physical avatars either when they see the need for one or when they are called upon under the right circumstances.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The honest answer is that I pretty much just made those terms up. Rakmou-leusan was derived from several words involving blood and violence (back when Rakmou-leusan was a war god in like, super super early drafting stages of SCP-2417) but I can't remember for the life of me what those were, and the rest of the Ortothan language is made up as I go along (haven't set it up as a conlang though — I'm not familiar with linguistics and don't trust myself to pull it off properly). Apologies if this does pose issue in translation.

item.content:encoded:
Super happy to see CotSH finally make it onto the main GoI listing. Overdue if you ask me, for the most creative and entertaining GoI that tragically few have heard of. I bet this new hub will go some ways towards fixing that though.

Tales of multiverse travelers moving down so many dimensions that they fall out of existence and into the Voru have been told, but the validity of these have been debated.

So, I like the really subtle reference to Pattern Screamers here, but on the other hand I kind of feel like Ortothans are in a position where they should have a fairly solid understanding of Pattern Screamers.

item.content:encoded:
This is a fucking wild moment for me. Don't even know what to say, so I may as well cut to the chase.

+ Thanks to (deep breath)...
- holy shit that's a lot of people
  • Shaggydredlocks: Without all of your crit on SCP-2417 the Church of the Second Hytoth would be absolutely nothing like how it is today. I can't give nowhere near enough credit for it.
  • LordStonefish: For writing for the group early in its development and helping me realize that this is something more people would want to write about.
  • Modern_Erasmus: The advice you gave me about focusing more on the alien side of the Church to make the group feel more unique was some of the best advice I've received and has massively influenced how I've written the group since.
  • Metaphysician: Your knack at worldbuilding has and always will be an inspiration for all of the Ortothan worldbuilding I write.
  • mlister: For always keeping me encouraged to keep pushing on with the group and for their feedback.
  • Rat Lord: HATEFUL STAR 2: APOCALYPSE BOOGALOO
  • Uncle Nicolini: For all of their edits to the layout of this hub, its CSS, and their advice on how to best present the information here. Without them this hub be nothing like how it is today.
  • OthellotheCat: For being the #1 Terzan 2 fanboy.
  • Panteradactyl: For coming up with ideas regarding alien cultures and concepts.
  • DrMacro and DrCendres: I can't express just how giddy I was when I saw your team's CotSH contest articles. Seriously. It made my day.
  • Taoka: For designing the Church logo based on my crummy sketches of it (I love your work on it so heckin' much).
  • All of this hub's critters: Elogee FishTruck, DrChandra, and the rest who gave it lookovers — can't remember everyone just yet.
  • And to everyone else who has expressed interest in the group along the way.
